v: The record of the genealogy[^1] of Jesus the Messiah,[^2] the son of David, the son of Abraham.[^3]
Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ.
Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.[^4]
Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ,
Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram.[^5]
Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζάρα ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀράμ,
Ram fathered Amminadab, Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών,
Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab,[^6] Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse.[^7]
Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βόες ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βόες δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί,
Jesse fathered King David. David[^8] fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah.[^9]
Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα. Δαυὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου,
Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph.[^10]
Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ,
Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.[^11]
Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν,
Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
Ὀζίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ, Ἰωαθὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχάζ, Ἀχὰζ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑζεκίαν,
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amos,[^12] and Amos fathered Josiah.
Ἑζεκίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μανασσῆ, Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσίαν,
Josiah fathered Jeconiah[^13] and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.[^14]
Ἰωσίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος.
After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.[^15]
Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβαβέλ,
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud,[^16] Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor.
Ζοροβαβὲλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ, Ἀβιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιακίμ, Ἐλιακὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀζώρ,
Azor fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud.
Ἀζὼρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαδώκ, Σαδὼκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχίμ, Ἀχὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιούδ,
Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob.
Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ματθάν, Ματθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ,
Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary. From her[^17] was born Jesus, who is called the Messiah.
Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός.
So there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen generations from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen generations from the exile to Babylon to the Messiah.[^18]
Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
This is how the birth of Jesus the Messiah[^19] came about. His mother Mary was engaged[^20] to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν. μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσήφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
Her husband Joseph was a righteous man and did not want to disgrace her publicly, so he decided to divorce her[^21] quietly.
Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν.

But when he had thought this over, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph son of David, don't be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, because what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου κατʼ ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυίδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου, τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου·
She will give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus,[^22] because he will save his people from their sins."
τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
All this took place so that what the Lord had said through the prophet would be fulfilled:
τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
"Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel,"[^23] which means "God is with us."
Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ· ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθʼ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.
When Joseph woke up from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his wife home.
ἐγερθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν αὐτῷ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου καὶ παρέλαβεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ·
He did not have sexual relations with her[^24] until she had given birth to a son,[^25] and he named him Jesus.
καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.

n.1: Literally "The book of the genesis". Greek *genesis* means origin or birth (as in verse 18). In the Greek Old Testament the same phrase introduces the record of Adam's descendants (Genesis 5:1; compare 2:4).
n.2: Or "Jesus Christ". Greek *christos*, "anointed one".
n.3: *Son* here means descendant.
n.4: Verses 2–6 follow the line in Ruth 4:18–22 and 1 Chronicles 1:34; 2:1–15. The names in verses 2–16 are spelled as in this translation's Old Testament; Matthew gives them in their Greek forms, such as *Phares* (Perez), *Zara* (Zerah) and *Hesrom* (Hezron). The notes mention the forms that differ more widely.
n.5: Greek *Aram* here and in verse 4. The Hebrew name is Ram (Ruth 4:19; 1 Chronicles 2:9–10).
n.6: The Old Testament does not name Salmon's wife. Rahab is the name of the woman of Jericho who hid the Israelite spies (Joshua 2; 6:25). Salmon is called Salma in 1 Chronicles 2:11 and Salmah in Ruth 4:20.
n.7: Greek *Boes* (Boaz) and *Iobed* (Obed).
n.8: Many manuscripts read "King David".
n.9: Literally "by her of Uriah", that is, Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11:3; 12:24).
n.10: Many manuscripts read *Asa*, the king's name in 1 Kings 15:8–24 and 1 Chronicles 3:10; also in verse 8. Asaph is also the name of a psalm writer (Psalms 50; 73–83).
n.11: Greek *Ozias*. Uzziah, also called Azariah (2 Kings 15:1–7; 1 Chronicles 3:12), was Joram's great-great-grandson: the list passes over Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah (1 Chronicles 3:11–12).
n.12: Many manuscripts read *Amon*, the king's name in 2 Kings 21:18–26 and 1 Chronicles 3:14; also later in the verse. Amos is also the name of a prophet.
n.13: Greek *Iechonias*. Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:6), was Josiah's grandson, the son of Jehoiakim (1 Chronicles 3:15–16).
n.14: Greek *metoikesia*, "removal, deportation"; also in verses 12 and 17. The people of Judah were taken to Babylon in the days of Jehoiachin and Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:10–16; 25:8–21).
n.15: Greek *Salathiel* and *Zorobabel*. In 1 Chronicles 3:17–19 Zerubbabel is the son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother; elsewhere he is called the son of Shealtiel (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1).
n.16: The names from Abiud to Jacob (verses 13–16) are not found in the Old Testament, which lists other descendants of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19–24).
n.17: *Her* is feminine in the Greek. Here the pattern "X fathered Y" changes, and Jesus is said to be born of Mary (verses 18–25).
n.18: Matthew arranges the genealogy in three sets of fourteen. As the names are listed, the first set has fourteen names (Abraham to David) and the second has fourteen (Solomon to Jeconiah, leaving out the kings mentioned in the note on verse 8). The third has thirteen (Shealtiel to Jesus) unless Jeconiah is counted again at its start. The letters of David's name in Hebrew (DWD) have the number values 4, 6 and 4, which add up to fourteen.
n.19: Some manuscripts read "the birth of the Messiah".
n.20: Or "betrothed", "pledged to be married". A betrothal was legally binding: Joseph is already called her husband (verse 19), and ending it required a divorce.
n.21: Literally "release her", the word used for divorce (5:31–32).
n.22: *Jesus* is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua (*Yeshua*), which means "The LORD saves". The LORD is God's personal name.
n.23: Isaiah 7:14. Matthew follows the Greek Septuagint, which has *parthenos*, "virgin", where the Hebrew has *almah*, "young woman", a girl old enough to marry. The Hebrew reads "she will call"; Matthew reads "they will call".
n.24: Literally "he was not knowing her", a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations.

v: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, in the days of King Herod,[^1] magi[^2] from the east arrived in Jerusalem
Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γεννηθέντος ἐν Βηθλέεμ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐν ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου τοῦ βασιλέως, ἰδοὺ μάγοι ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα
and asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star at its rising[^3] and have come to worship him."[^4]
λέγοντες· Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ τεχθεὶς βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; εἴδομεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀστέρα ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ.
When King Herod heard this, he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.
ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης ἐταράχθη καὶ πᾶσα Ἱεροσόλυμα μετʼ αὐτοῦ,
He called together all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.
καὶ συναγαγὼν πάντας τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ γραμματεῖς τοῦ λαοῦ ἐπυνθάνετο παρʼ αὐτῶν ποῦ ὁ χριστὸς γεννᾶται.
They told him, "In Bethlehem in Judea, because this is what was written through the prophet:
οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἐν Βηθλέεμ τῆς Ἰουδαίας· οὕτως γὰρ γέγραπται διὰ τοῦ προφήτου·
'And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"[^5]
Καὶ σύ, Βηθλέεμ γῆ Ἰούδα, οὐδαμῶς ἐλαχίστη εἶ ἐν τοῖς ἡγεμόσιν Ἰούδα· ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται ἡγούμενος, ὅστις ποιμανεῖ τὸν λαόν μου τὸν Ἰσραήλ.
Then Herod secretly called the magi and found out from them exactly when the star had appeared.
Τότε Ἡρῴδης λάθρᾳ καλέσας τοὺς μάγους ἠκρίβωσεν παρʼ αὐτῶν τὸν χρόνον τοῦ φαινομένου ἀστέρος,
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report to me, so that I too may come and worship him."
καὶ πέμψας αὐτοὺς εἰς Βηθλέεμ εἶπεν· Πορευθέντες ἐξετάσατε ἀκριβῶς περὶ τοῦ παιδίου· ἐπὰν δὲ εὕρητε, ἀπαγγείλατέ μοι, ὅπως κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν προσκυνήσω αὐτῷ.
After listening to the king, they set out. And there was the star they had seen at its rising, going ahead of them, until it came and stopped over the place where the child was.
οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες τοῦ βασιλέως ἐπορεύθησαν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ὁ ἀστὴρ ὃν εἶδον ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ προῆγεν αὐτούς, ἕως ἐλθὼν ἐστάθη ἐπάνω οὗ ἦν τὸ παιδίον.
When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.[^6]
ἰδόντες δὲ τὸν ἀστέρα ἐχάρησαν χαρὰν μεγάλην σφόδρα.
They went into the house and saw the child with his mother Mary, and they fell down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasure chests and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.[^7]
καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἶδον τὸ παιδίον μετὰ Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ πεσόντες προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνοίξαντες τοὺς θησαυροὺς αὐτῶν προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δῶρα, χρυσὸν καὶ λίβανον καὶ σμύρναν.
And since they had been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another route.
καὶ χρηματισθέντες κατʼ ὄναρ μὴ ἀνακάμψαι πρὸς Ἡρῴδην διʼ ἄλλης ὁδοῦ ἀνεχώρησαν εἰς τὴν χώραν αὐτῶν.

After they had gone, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is going to search for the child to kill him."

Ἀναχωρησάντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου φαίνεται κατʼ ὄναρ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ λέγων· Ἐγερθεὶς παράλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ φεῦγε εἰς Αἴγυπτον, καὶ ἴσθι ἐκεῖ ἕως ἂν εἴπω σοι· μέλλει γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ζητεῖν τὸ παιδίον τοῦ ἀπολέσαι αὐτό.
So Joseph got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt.
ὁ δὲ ἐγερθεὶς παρέλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς καὶ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς Αἴγυπτον,
He stayed there until the death of Herod. This was so that what the Lord had said through the prophet would be fulfilled: "Out of Egypt I called my son."[^8]
καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἕως τῆς τελευτῆς Ἡρῴδου· ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἐκάλεσα τὸν υἱόν μου.

When Herod saw that he had been tricked by the magi, he was furious. He sent men to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and all its surrounding region who were two years old and under, according to the time he had found out exactly from the magi.

Τότε Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν ὅτι ἐνεπαίχθη ὑπὸ τῶν μάγων ἐθυμώθη λίαν, καὶ ἀποστείλας ἀνεῖλεν πάντας τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς ἐν Βηθλέεμ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὁρίοις αὐτῆς ἀπὸ διετοῦς καὶ κατωτέρω, κατὰ τὸν χρόνον ὃν ἠκρίβωσεν παρὰ τῶν μάγων.
Then what had been spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled:
τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
"A voice was heard in Ramah,[^9] weeping and great mourning: Rachel weeping for her children,[^10] and she refused to be comforted, because they are no more."[^11]
Φωνὴ ἐν Ῥαμὰ ἠκούσθη, κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὀδυρμὸς πολύς· Ῥαχὴλ κλαίουσα τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν παρακληθῆναι ὅτι οὐκ εἰσίν.
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
Τελευτήσαντος δὲ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου φαίνεται κατʼ ὄναρ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ
and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, because those who were seeking the child's life are dead."
λέγων· Ἐγερθεὶς παράλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πορεύου εἰς γῆν Ἰσραήλ, τεθνήκασιν γὰρ οἱ ζητοῦντες τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ παιδίου.
So Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and went into the land of Israel.
ὁ δὲ ἐγερθεὶς παρέλαβε τὸ παιδίον καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς γῆν Ἰσραήλ.
But when he heard that Archelaus[^12] was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. And having been warned in a dream, he went away to the region of Galilee.
ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἀρχέλαος βασιλεύει τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἀντὶ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ἡρῴδου ἐφοβήθη ἐκεῖ ἀπελθεῖν· χρηματισθεὶς δὲ κατʼ ὄναρ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη τῆς Γαλιλαίας,
He went and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken through the prophets would be fulfilled: "He will be called a Nazarene."[^13]
καὶ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς πόλιν λεγομένην Ναζαρέτ, ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τῶν προφητῶν ὅτι Ναζωραῖος κληθήσεται.

n.1: Herod the Great, who ruled Judea as king under the Romans from 37 to 4 BC.
n.2: Greek *magoi*, experts in astrology and the interpretation of dreams, probably from Persia or Babylonia. Traditionally "wise men".
n.3: Or "in the east"; also in verse 9.
n.4: Or "pay him homage"; also in verses 8 and 11. Greek *proskyneo*, to bow down before someone, a king or God.
n.5: Micah 5:1 (5:2 in most English Bibles), quoted freely, with words from 2 Samuel 5:2 ("You will shepherd my people Israel"). Micah's Hebrew reads "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the clans of Judah, from you one will come out for me to be ruler in Israel."
n.6: Literally "they rejoiced with very great joy".
n.7: Frankincense and myrrh are fragrant resins from trees, used for incense, perfume and medicine.
n.8: Hosea 11:1. Matthew follows the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads "out of Egypt I called his children".
n.9: Many manuscripts add "lamentation,".
n.10: Rachel, the mother of Joseph and Benjamin, was buried on the road to Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19).
n.11: Jeremiah 31:15. Matthew's Greek is shorter than the Hebrew, which reads "lamentation and bitter weeping" and "she refuses to be comforted for her children".
n.12: A son of Herod. He ruled Judea, Samaria and Idumea from 4 BC to AD 6, with the title of ethnarch ("ruler of a people"), not king.
n.13: No passage in the Old Testament has these words. *Nazarene* may recall the Hebrew *netser*, "branch" (Isaiah 11:1), or *nazir*, "Nazirite", one set apart to God (Judges 13:5–7). Or "that he would be called a Nazarene".

v: In those days John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming
Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις παραγίνεται Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς κηρύσσων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
and saying, "Repent,[^1] for the kingdom of heaven[^2] has come near."
καὶ λέγων· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
This is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke about when he said: "A voice is shouting in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way for the Lord; make his paths straight.'"[^3]
οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ῥηθεὶς διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.
John wore clothing made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist,[^4] and his food was locusts and wild honey.
αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάννης εἶχεν τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τριχῶν καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, ἡ δὲ τροφὴ ἦν αὐτοῦ ἀκρίδες καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
Then the people of Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan went out to him.
τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου,
They confessed their sins and were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees[^5] coming to his baptism, he said to them, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Ἰδὼν δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων ἐρχομένους ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
Produce fruit, then, that fits your repentance.
ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας
And don't think you can say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.
The ax is already lying at the root of the trees. So every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
ἤδη δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who comes after me is more powerful than I am. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.[^6]
Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί·
His winnowing fork[^7] is in his hand. He will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but he will burn up the chaff with fire that never goes out."
οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.
Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.
Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
But John tried to stop him. "I need to be baptized by you," he said, "and do you come to me?"
ὁ δὲ Ἰωάννης διεκώλυεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;
Jesus answered him, "Let it be so for now. It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness[^8] in this way." Then John allowed him.
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἄφες ἄρτι, οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτόν.
When Jesus had been baptized, he came up from the water at once. Just then the heavens were opened,[^9] and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and coming on him.
βαπτισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὐθὺς ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί, καὶ εἶδεν πνεῦμα θεοῦ καταβαῖνον ὡσεὶ περιστερὰν ἐρχόμενον ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
And a voice from the heavens said, "This is my Son, whom I love. I am delighted with him."[^10]
καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα.

n.1: Greek *metanoeo*, to change one's mind and way of life, to turn around. Also in verses 8 and 11 (*metanoia*, "repentance").
n.2: Literally "the kingdom of the heavens", Matthew's usual phrase. Many Jews of the time spoke of "heaven" instead of naming God. Mark and Luke have "the kingdom of God".
n.3: Isaiah 40:3. Matthew follows the Septuagint, which joins "in the wilderness" to the voice; the Hebrew reads "A voice is shouting: 'In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD.'" In Isaiah's Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD").
n.4: Elijah was dressed in the same way (2 Kings 1:8).
n.5: The Pharisees were a movement of teachers and laypeople devoted to keeping the Law of Moses and the traditions that explained it. The Sadducees were a party of priests and leading families, who accepted only the written Law and did not believe in the resurrection (22:23).
n.6: Many manuscripts leave out "and fire".
n.7: A wooden fork for tossing threshed grain into the air, so that the wind would blow the chaff away.
n.8: Or "to do everything that is right".
n.9: Many manuscripts read "opened to him".
n.10: Or "This is my beloved Son; I take great pleasure in him." Compare Psalm 2:7; Isaiah 42:1.

v: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tested[^1] by the devil.
Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσεράκοντα ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.
The tempter came and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.
Jesus answered, "It is written: 'People do not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"[^2]
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος θεοῦ.
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point[^3] of the temple,
Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ,

and he said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. For it is written: 'He will command his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"[^4]
καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
Jesus said to him, "It is also written: 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"[^5]
ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάλιν γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν
And he said to him, "I will give you all these things if you will fall down and worship me."
καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.
Then Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan![^6] For it is written: 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.'"[^7]
τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
Then the devil left him, and angels came and took care of him.
τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
When Jesus heard that John had been arrested,[^8] he withdrew to Galilee.
Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάννης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ·
so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled:
ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:[^9]
Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλίμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν,
the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and on those sitting in the land and shadow of death a light has dawned."[^10]
ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.
From that time Jesus began to proclaim, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς, Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·
He said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will make you fish for people."
καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
At once they left their nets and followed him.
οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets, and he called them.
Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς, Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
At once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ.

The news about him spread through all Syria, and people brought to him all who were ill, suffering from various diseases and pains: those possessed by demons, those who had seizures,[^11] and the paralyzed. And he healed them.

καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν· καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους, δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis,[^12] Jerusalem, Judea, and the region beyond the Jordan.
καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.

n.1: Or "tempted". The Greek word means both. Also in verse 3, "the tempter".
n.2: Deuteronomy 8:3. Matthew follows the Septuagint, which has "every word" and "God"; the Hebrew reads "everything that comes from the mouth of the LORD".
n.3: Literally "the little wing", perhaps a high corner of the temple's outer wall.
n.4: Psalm 91:11–12, leaving out "to guard you in all your ways".
n.5: Deuteronomy 6:16. In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD"); also in verse 10.
n.6: Many manuscripts read "Get behind me, Satan!"
n.7: Deuteronomy 6:13. The Hebrew reads "Fear the LORD your God. Serve him"; Matthew has "worship" and "only", in a form close to the Septuagint.
n.8: Literally "handed over".
n.9: Or "of the Gentiles".
n.10: Isaiah 8:23–9:1 (9:1–2 in most English Bibles), in a shortened form. Isaiah's Hebrew has "walked in darkness" and "the land of deep darkness" (traditionally "the shadow of death").
n.11: Literally "those who were moonstruck", probably people with epilepsy.
n.12: "The Ten Towns", a group of Greek cities east of the Jordan.

v: When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up on the mountain. After he sat down, his disciples came to him,
Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
and he began to teach them,[^1] saying:
καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
"Blessed[^2] are the poor in spirit, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.[^3]
μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.[^4]
μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,[^5] for they will be filled.
μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.[^6]
μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.[^7]
μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
"Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me.
μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθʼ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ.
Rejoice and be glad, because your reward in heaven is great. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
"You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its taste,[^8] how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by people.
Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται; εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
"You are the light of the world. A town set on a hill cannot be hidden.
Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου. οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
People do not light a lamp and put it under a basket,[^9] but on a lampstand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
In the same way, let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and praise your Father in heaven.
οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
"Don't think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets.[^10] I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.
Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
Truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not the smallest letter or the least stroke of a letter[^11] will pass from the Law until everything has taken place.
ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.

So whoever breaks[^12] one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
For I tell you, unless your righteousness goes far beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
"You have heard that it was said to the people of long ago,[^13] 'You must not murder,' and 'Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.'[^14]
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δʼ ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with their brother[^15] will be liable to judgment. Whoever says to their brother, 'Raca,'[^16] will be liable to the council.[^17] And whoever says, 'You fool!' will be liable to the fire of hell.[^18]

ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
"So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ,
leave your gift there in front of the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.

Come to terms quickly with your opponent while you are still with him on the way to court.[^19] Otherwise your opponent may hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
Truly I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid the last penny.[^20]
ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
"You have heard that it was said, 'You must not commit adultery.'[^21]
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman[^22] with desire for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
If your right eye causes you to stumble,[^23] tear it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go into hell.
καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
"It was also said, 'Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.'[^24]
Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality,[^25] causes her to commit adultery,[^26] and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
"Again, you have heard that it was said to the people of long ago, 'Do not swear falsely, but carry out the oaths you have made to the Lord.'[^27]
Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
But I tell you, do not swear at all: not by heaven, because it is God's throne,
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
or by the earth, because it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.[^28]
μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
And do not swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
Let what you say be simply 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no'.[^29] Anything more than this comes from the evil one.[^30]
ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
"You have heard that it was said, 'Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.'[^31]
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
But I tell you, do not resist an evil person.[^32] If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other cheek to him as well.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλʼ ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
If anyone wants to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.[^33]
καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
If anyone forces you to go one mile,[^34] go with him two.
καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο.
Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
"You have heard that it was said, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'[^35]
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,[^36]
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
so that you may be children[^37] of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
If you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don't even the tax collectors do the same?
ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
And if you greet only your brothers,[^38] what are you doing more than others? Don't even the Gentiles do the same?
καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
So be perfect,[^39] as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.

n.1: Literally "opening his mouth, he taught them".
n.2: Greek *makarioi*, "blessed, happy, fortunate": those whom God favors. Also in verses 4–11.
n.3: Compare Isaiah 61:1–3, with its good news for the poor and comfort for all who mourn.
n.4: Or "the meek", "the humble"; *the earth*: or "the land". Compare Psalm 37:11, "But the humble will inherit the land."
n.5: Or "for justice", "for what is right".
n.6: Compare Psalm 24:3–4.
n.7: Literally "sons of God".
n.8: The Greek verb also means "become foolish".
n.9: Greek *modios*, a container for measuring grain, holding about 8 liters (2 gallons).
n.10: *The Law or the Prophets*: the Hebrew scriptures.
n.11: Literally "not one *iota* or one horn". The *iota* is the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet (compare the Hebrew *yod*), and the "horn" is a tiny stroke that tells one letter from another.
n.12: Or "sets aside", "annuls".
n.13: Or "by the people of long ago"; also in verse 33.
n.14: Exodus 20:13; Deuteronomy 5:17. The second sentence sums up laws such as Exodus 21:12.
n.15: Or "brother or sister", a fellow member of God's people; also in verses 23–24. Many manuscripts add "without cause".
n.17: Greek *synedrion*, a council of judges; in Jerusalem, the Sanhedrin, the supreme Jewish council.
n.18: Literally "the Gehenna of fire". Greek *Gehenna*, from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, used as a name for the place of final judgment. Also in verses 29–30.
n.20: Greek *kodrantes*, from the Latin *quadrans*, a small Roman coin worth 1/64 of a denarius.
n.22: Or "a married woman". Greek *gyne* means both "woman" and "wife".
n.25: Literally "except for a matter of *porneia*", a general word for sexual immorality.
n.26: Or "makes her the victim of adultery".
n.27: Compare Leviticus 19:12; Numbers 30:3 (30:2 in most English Bibles); Deuteronomy 23:22 (23:21 in most English Bibles). In the Hebrew, "the Lord" is God's personal name, YHWH ("the LORD").
n.28: Isaiah 66:1; Psalm 48:3 (48:2 in most English Bibles).
n.29: That is, a plain yes or no, without an oath.
n.33: The tunic was worn next to the skin; the cloak was the outer garment, which a poor person also used as a blanket at night (Exodus 22:25–26; 22:26–27 in most English Bibles).
n.34: Greek *milion*, a Roman mile, about 1,480 meters (4,860 feet). Soldiers and officials could force people to carry loads for them.
n.35: Leviticus 19:18. The words "and hate your enemy" are not found in the Old Testament.
n.36: Many manuscripts read "love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you".
n.38: Or "brothers and sisters". Many manuscripts read "your friends" and, later in the verse, "the tax collectors".

v: "Be careful not to practice your righteousness[^1] in front of people in order to be seen by them. If you do, you have no reward from your Father in heaven.
Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

"So when you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites[^2] do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be praised by people. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.[^3]
Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.[^4]
ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.

"And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, because they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so that people may see them. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.

Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
"When you pray, do not babble on like the Gentiles, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.
Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·
Do not be like them, for your Father[^5] knows what you need before you ask him.
μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
"This, then, is how you should pray: 'Our Father in heaven, may your name be honored as holy.
Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
May your kingdom come, may your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς·
Give us today our daily bread.[^6]
τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
And forgive us our debts,[^7] as we also have forgiven our debtors.[^8]
καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
And do not bring us into testing,[^9] but rescue us from the evil one.'[^10]
καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
For if you forgive others their wrongdoings, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
But if you do not forgive others,[^11] your Father will not forgive your wrongdoings either.
ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
"When you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites. They disfigure their faces so that people may see that they are fasting.[^12] Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full.
Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
so that your fasting may be seen not by people but by your Father, who is in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
"Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust[^13] destroy, and where thieves break in[^14] and steal.
Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
"The eye is the lamp of the body. So if your eye is healthy,[^15] your whole body will be full of light.
Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
But if your eye is bad,[^16] your whole body will be full of darkness. So if the light in you is darkness, how great that darkness is!
ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
"No one can serve[^17] two masters. Either they will hate the one and love the other, or they will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and money.[^18]
Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
"That is why I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat,[^19] or about your body, what you will wear. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
Look at the birds of the sky. They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you worth much more than they are?
ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
Which of you by worrying can add one cubit[^20] to your span of life?
τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
"And why do you worry about clothing? Consider how the lilies[^21] of the field grow. They do not labor or spin.
καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won't he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
So do not worry, saying, 'What will we eat?' or 'What will we drink?' or 'What will we wear?'
μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
But seek first the kingdom[^22] and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.

n.1: Many manuscripts read "your acts of charity".
n.2: Greek *hypokrites*, an actor, someone playing a part; also in verses 5 and 16.
n.3: Greek *apecho*, a word used on receipts: "paid in full". Also in verses 5 and 16.
n.4: Many manuscripts add "openly"; also in verse 6.
n.5: Some manuscripts read "God your Father".
n.6: Greek *epiousios*, a rare word whose meaning is uncertain. It may mean "for the coming day" (tomorrow's bread, or the bread of the age to come), "needed for existence", or "for today". "Daily" is the traditional rendering. Jerome (about AD 400) reported that a Hebrew gospel known to him had *mahar*, "tomorrow".
n.7: That is, the wrongs we have done, our sins (verses 14–15; compare Luke 11:4).
n.8: Many manuscripts read "as we also forgive our debtors".
n.9: Or "temptation".
n.10: Or "from evil". Many manuscripts add "For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen." Compare 1 Chronicles 29:11.
n.11: Many manuscripts add "their wrongdoings".
n.12: There is a play on words in the Greek: they make their faces "disappear" so that they may "appear" to people as fasting.
n.13: Literally "eating", whether by insects or by rust; also in verse 20.
n.14: Literally "dig through", that is, through the mud-brick wall of a house; also in verse 20.
n.15: Literally "single": sound, clear, and also generous.
n.16: Literally "evil", which can also mean "unhealthy". An "evil eye" was an expression for envy or stinginess (20:15).
n.17: Or "be a slave to"; also later in the verse.
n.19: Many manuscripts add "or what you will drink" (compare verse 31). The SBLGNT leaves it out, following a marginal reading of Westcott and Hort.
n.20: About 18 inches (45 cm). *Span of life*: or "height".
n.22: Many manuscripts read "the kingdom of God".

v: "Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
For you will be judged by the judgment you use, and the measure you use will be used to measure you.
ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's[^1] eye but do not notice the log in your own eye?
τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when there is a log in your own eye?
ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
You hypocrite! First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
"Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls in front of pigs. Otherwise they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.
Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
"Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
Or which of you, if your son asks you for bread, will give him a stone?
ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον— μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
Or if he asks for a fish, will you give him a snake?
ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει— μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
"So in everything, do to others what you want them to do to you, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
"Enter through the narrow gate. For the gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to destruction, and many go in through it.[^2]
Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι διʼ αὐτῆς·
For the gate is narrow and the road is hard[^3] that leads to life, and only a few find it.[^4]
ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
"Watch out for false prophets. They come to you in sheep's clothing, but inside they are ravenous wolves.
Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
You will recognize them by their fruit. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς. μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, but a rotten tree produces bad fruit.
οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, and a rotten tree cannot produce good fruit.
οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
So then, you will recognize them by their fruit.
ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
"Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλʼ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
On that day many will say to me, 'Lord, Lord, didn't we prophesy in your name, and drive out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?'
πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
Then I will tell them plainly, 'I never knew you. Depart from me, you who practice lawlessness!'[^5]
καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
"So everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat against that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock.
καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell, and its fall was great."
καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
When Jesus had finished saying these things,[^6] the crowds were amazed at his teaching,
Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
because he taught them like someone with authority, not like their scribes.
ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.

n.1: Or "brother or sister"; also in verses 4–5.
n.2: Some manuscripts read "For wide and broad is the road".
n.3: Or "constricted". The Greek word is related to *thlipsis*, "trouble, persecution".
n.4: Many manuscripts read "How narrow is the gate and how hard the road that leads to life, and only a few find it!"
n.5: Psalm 6:9 (6:8 in most English Bibles): "Depart from me, all you evildoers."
n.6: Matthew ends each of Jesus' five long discourses with similar words (11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1).

v: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
Καταβάντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί.
Just then a man with a skin disease[^1] came and knelt before him[^2] and said, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
καὶ ἰδοὺ λεπρὸς προσελθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
Jesus reached out his hand and touched him. "I am willing," he said. "Be made clean!" At once he was cleansed of his skin disease.
καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἐκαθαρίσθη αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα.
Then Jesus said to him, "See that you tell no one. But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as evidence for them."[^3]
καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅρα μηδενὶ εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκον τὸ δῶρον ὃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion[^4] came to him, pleading with him
Εἰσελθόντος δὲ αὐτοῦ εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἑκατόνταρχος παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν
and saying, "Lord, my servant[^5] is lying at home paralyzed, suffering terribly."
καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ὁ παῖς μου βέβληται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ παραλυτικός, δεινῶς βασανιζόμενος.
Jesus said to him, "I will come and heal him."[^6]
καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἐγὼ ἐλθὼν θεραπεύσω αὐτόν.
The centurion answered, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἑκατόνταρχος ἔφη· Κύριε, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς ἵνα μου ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην εἰσέλθῃς· ἀλλὰ μόνον εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήσεται ὁ παῖς μου·
For I too am a man under authority,[^7] with soldiers under me. I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my servant,[^8] 'Do this,' and he does it."
καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν, ἔχων ὑπʼ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those who were following him, "Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.[^9]
ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς ἀκολουθοῦσιν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, παρʼ οὐδενὶ τοσαύτην πίστιν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ εὗρον.
I tell you, many will come from east and west and will recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν ἥξουσιν καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται μετὰ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν·
but the heirs of the kingdom[^10] will be thrown out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth."
οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας ἐκβληθήσονται εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
Then Jesus said to the centurion, "Go. Let it be done for you as you have believed." And the servant was healed at that very hour.
καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ· Ὕπαγε, ὡς ἐπίστευσας γενηθήτω σοι· καὶ ἰάθη ὁ παῖς ἐν τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.
When Jesus came into Peter's house, he saw Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
Καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Πέτρου εἶδεν τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτοῦ βεβλημένην καὶ πυρέσσουσαν·
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began to serve him.
καὶ ἥψατο τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ διηκόνει αὐτῷ.
That evening people brought to him many who were possessed by demons. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick,
Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δαιμονιζομένους πολλούς· καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὰ πνεύματα λόγῳ, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ἐθεράπευσεν·
so that what had been spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled: "He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases."[^11]
ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Αὐτὸς τὰς ἀσθενείας ἡμῶν ἔλαβεν καὶ τὰς νόσους ἐβάστασεν.
When Jesus saw the large crowds[^12] around him, he gave orders to cross to the other side.
Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πολλοὺς ὄχλους περὶ αὐτὸν ἐκέλευσεν ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
A scribe came and said to him, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς γραμματεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ.
Jesus said to him, "Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man[^13] has nowhere to lay his head."
καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.
Another of the disciples said to him, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
ἕτερος δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι πρῶτον ἀπελθεῖν καὶ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.
But Jesus said to him, "Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead."
ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι, καὶ ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς.
When he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
Καὶ ἐμβάντι αὐτῷ εἰς πλοῖον ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
Suddenly a great storm[^14] arose on the sea, so that the boat was being swamped by the waves. But Jesus was asleep.
καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς μέγας ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ὥστε τὸ πλοῖον καλύπτεσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκάθευδεν.
They went and woke him, saying, "Lord, save us! We are about to die!"
καὶ προσελθόντες ἤγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, σῶσον, ἀπολλύμεθα.
He said to them, "Why are you so afraid, you of little faith?" Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε, ὀλιγόπιστοι; τότε ἐγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τοῖς ἀνέμοις καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.
The men were amazed and said, "What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Ποταπός ἐστιν οὗτος ὅτι καὶ οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ ἡ θάλασσα αὐτῷ ὑπακούουσιν;
When he came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes,[^15] two men possessed by demons came out of the tombs to meet him. They were so violent that no one could pass along that road.
Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πέραν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γαδαρηνῶν ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ δύο δαιμονιζόμενοι ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἐξερχόμενοι, χαλεποὶ λίαν ὥστε μὴ ἰσχύειν τινὰ παρελθεῖν διὰ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἐκείνης.
Suddenly they cried out, "What do you want with us,[^16] Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?"
καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔκραξαν λέγοντες· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ; ἦλθες ὧδε πρὸ καιροῦ βασανίσαι ἡμᾶς;
Some distance from them a large herd of pigs was feeding.
ἦν δὲ μακρὰν ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀγέλη χοίρων πολλῶν βοσκομένη.
The demons begged him, "If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
οἱ δὲ δαίμονες παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἐκβάλλεις ἡμᾶς, ἀπόστειλον ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀγέλην τῶν χοίρων.
He said to them, "Go!" So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the water.
καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε. οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἀπῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους· καὶ ἰδοὺ ὥρμησεν πᾶσα ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ ἀπέθανον ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν.
The men who tended the pigs ran off, went into the town, and reported everything, including what had happened to the men possessed by demons.
οἱ δὲ βόσκοντες ἔφυγον, καὶ ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν πάντα καὶ τὰ τῶν δαιμονιζομένων.
Then the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
καὶ ἰδοὺ πᾶσα ἡ πόλις ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ὑπάντησιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν παρεκάλεσαν ὅπως μεταβῇ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.

n.1: Greek *lepros*, traditionally "leper". The word covered various skin diseases, not only what is now called leprosy.
n.2: Or "worshiped him". Greek *proskyneo*; see 2:2.
n.3: Or "as a testimony against them". The offering is described in Leviticus 14:1–32.
n.4: A Roman officer in command of about a hundred soldiers.
n.5: Greek *pais*, "boy", which can mean a son or a servant; also in verses 8 and 13.
n.6: Or "Am I to come and heal him?"
n.7: Some manuscripts add "appointed".
n.8: Or "slave". Greek *doulos*, a different word from the one in verses 6, 8 and 13.
n.9: Many manuscripts read "not even in Israel have I found such great faith".
n.10: Literally "the sons of the kingdom", those who expected to belong to it.
n.11: Isaiah 53:4, translated from the Hebrew. The Septuagint reads "he bears our sins".
n.12: Some manuscripts read "a crowd".
n.13: A title Jesus uses for himself in all four Gospels. It recalls "one like a son of man" in Daniel 7:13, and in Hebrew idiom it can also mean simply "a human being".
n.14: Greek *seismos*, "shaking", the usual word for an earthquake.
n.15: Many manuscripts read "Gergesenes". Gadara was a town of the Decapolis, southeast of the Sea of Galilee. Mark 5:1 has "Gerasenes".
n.16: Literally "What to us and to you?", an idiom: "What do we have to do with you?"

v: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to his own town.
Καὶ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον διεπέρασεν καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν ἰδίαν πόλιν.
Just then some people brought to him a paralyzed man lying on a stretcher. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, "Take heart, son;[^1] your sins are forgiven."
Καὶ ἰδοὺ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παραλυτικὸν ἐπὶ κλίνης βεβλημένον. καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Θάρσει, τέκνον· ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
Then some of the scribes said to themselves, "This man is blaspheming!"
καὶ ἰδού τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτος βλασφημεῖ.
Knowing[^2] their thoughts, Jesus said, "Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
καὶ εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἱνατί ἐνθυμεῖσθε πονηρὰ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
τί γάρ ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—then he said to the paralyzed man—"get up, pick up your stretcher, and go home."
ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— τότε λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἐγερθεὶς ἆρόν σου τὴν κλίνην καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
And the man got up and went home.
καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe,[^3] and they praised God, who had given such authority to human beings.
ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐφοβήθησαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν τὸν δόντα ἐξουσίαν τοιαύτην τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
As Jesus walked on from there, he saw a man named Matthew[^4] sitting at the tax booth. "Follow me," he told him. And Matthew got up and followed him.
Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Μαθθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι· καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
Later, as Jesus was having a meal in the house,[^5] many tax collectors and sinners came and were eating with Jesus and his disciples.
Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
When the Pharisees saw this, they asked his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;
When he heard this, he said, "Healthy people don't need a doctor; sick people do.
ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας εἶπεν· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες.
Go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice.'[^6] For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."[^7]
πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν· οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.
Then John's disciples came to him and asked, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast often,[^8] but your disciples do not fast?"
Τότε προσέρχονται αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου λέγοντες· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύομεν πολλά, οἱ δὲ μαθηταί σου οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
Jesus said to them, "Can the wedding guests[^9] mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος πενθεῖν ἐφʼ ὅσον μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ὁ νυμφίος; ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν.
"No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch pulls away from the garment, and the tear gets worse.
οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐπιβάλλει ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπὶ ἱματίῳ παλαιῷ· αἴρει γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
Neither do people pour new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise the skins burst, the wine spills out, and the skins are ruined. No, they pour new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved."
οὐδὲ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, ῥήγνυνται οἱ ἀσκοί, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἐκχεῖται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπόλλυνται· ἀλλὰ βάλλουσιν οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς, καὶ ἀμφότεροι συντηροῦνται.
While he was saying these things to them, a leader[^10] came and knelt before him and said, "My daughter has just died. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν· ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπʼ αὐτήν, καὶ ζήσεται.
Jesus got up and followed him, and so did his disciples.
καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
Just then a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge[^11] of his cloak,
Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·
for she said to herself, "If I can just touch his cloak, I will be healed."
ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ· Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.
Jesus turned, and when he saw her, he said, "Take heart, daughter. Your faith has healed you."[^12] And the woman was healed from that hour.
ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Θάρσει, θύγατερ· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ ἐσώθη ἡ γυνὴ ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
When Jesus came into the leader's house and saw the flute players[^13] and the crowd making a commotion,
καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς αὐλητὰς καὶ τὸν ὄχλον θορυβούμενον
he said, "Go away. The girl is not dead but asleep." And they laughed at him.
ἔλεγεν· Ἀναχωρεῖτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν τὸ κοράσιον ἀλλὰ καθεύδει· καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ.
But when the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
ὅτε δὲ ἐξεβλήθη ὁ ὄχλος, εἰσελθὼν ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἠγέρθη τὸ κοράσιον.
The news of this spread through all that region.
καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ φήμη αὕτη εἰς ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἐκείνην.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"[^14]
Καὶ παράγοντι ἐκεῖθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ δύο τυφλοὶ κράζοντες καὶ λέγοντες· Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὲ Δαυίδ.
When he had gone into the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus asked them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" "Yes, Lord," they said to him.
ἐλθόντι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ τυφλοί, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πιστεύετε ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε.
Then he touched their eyes and said, "Let it be done for you according to your faith."
τότε ἥψατο τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν λέγων· Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν γενηθήτω ὑμῖν.
And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, "See that no one knows about this."
καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί. καὶ ἐνεβριμήθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε μηδεὶς γινωσκέτω·
But they went out and spread the news about him all through that region.
οἱ δὲ ἐξελθόντες διεφήμισαν αὐτὸν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ ἐκείνῃ.
As they were going out, some people brought to him a man who could not speak[^15] and was possessed by a demon.
Αὐτῶν δὲ ἐξερχομένων ἰδοὺ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπον κωφὸν δαιμονιζόμενον·
When the demon had been driven out, the man who could not speak began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!"
καὶ ἐκβληθέντος τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι λέγοντες· Οὐδέποτε ἐφάνη οὕτως ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ.
But the Pharisees said, "He drives out demons by the ruler of the demons."
οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον· Ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness.[^16]
Καὶ περιῆγεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς πόλεις πάσας καὶ τὰς κώμας, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.[^17]
Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἐσπλαγχνίσθη περὶ αὐτῶν ὅτι ἦσαν ἐσκυλμένοι καὶ ἐρριμμένοι ὡσεὶ πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα.
Then he said to his disciples, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
τότε λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι·
So ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest."
δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐκβάλῃ ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.

n.1: Literally "child", an affectionate form of address.
n.2: Many manuscripts read "Seeing".
n.3: Literally "they were afraid". Many manuscripts read "they were amazed".
n.4: Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 call the tax collector Levi.
n.5: Literally "in the house", perhaps Matthew's house or the one where Jesus was staying.
n.6: Hosea 6:6. Matthew follows the Septuagint, which has "mercy" where the Hebrew has *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.7: Many manuscripts add "to repentance".
n.8: Some manuscripts leave out "often".
n.9: Literally "the sons of the bridechamber".
n.10: Greek *archon*, "ruler, leader"; also in verse 23.
n.11: Or "the tassel". Jewish men wore tassels on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38–39).
n.12: Or "has saved you". The Greek verb *sozo* means both; also in verse 21, "healed", and later in this verse.
n.13: Musicians hired to play at funerals.
n.14: A title of the Messiah, the descendant of David (1:1; compare 2 Samuel 7:12–16).
n.15: Greek *kophos*, which can mean unable to speak or unable to hear; also in verse 33.

v: Jesus called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ,
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;[^1]
Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος,
Simon the Cananaean,[^2] and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.
Jesus sent out these twelve with these instructions: "Do not go among the Gentiles,[^3] and do not enter any town of the Samaritans.
Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
As you go, proclaim this message: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Heal the sick, raise the dead,[^4] cleanse those with skin diseases,[^5] drive out demons. You received without paying; give without being paid.
ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
Do not get any gold or silver or copper to put in your belts,
μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν,
or a bag for the journey, or two tunics, or sandals, or a walking stick. For the worker deserves his food.
μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
"Whatever town or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.
As you enter the house, greet it.[^6]
εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·
If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it. But if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπʼ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.
And if anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that house or town.
καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.
Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah[^7] on the day of judgment than for that town.
ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
"Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.
Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.
But watch out for people, for they will hand you over to councils[^8] and flog you in their synagogues.
προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·
You will be brought before governors and kings because of me, to bear witness to them and to the Gentiles.
καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
When they hand you over, do not worry about how to speak or what to say. What you are to say will be given to you at that time.
ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε·
For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.
"Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.
